title: A clock offset masquerading as a speed anomaly
promptMarkdown: Stationary detectors A and B are separated by $900\,\mathrm m$ in one inertial frame. Use $c=300\,\mathrm m/\mu\mathrm s$ for this exercise. A emits a pulse at $2.0\,\mu\mathrm s$ on its clock; B reflects it immediately; A receives it at $8.0\,\mu\mathrm s$. B displays $5.4\,\mu\mathrm s$ at reflection. A particle later passes A at $10.0\,\mu\mathrm s$ and B at displayed time $15.4\,\mu\mathrm s$. Determine B's offset, the corrected particle speed, and the false speed inferred without the correction. Explain what was assumed in synchronising the clocks.
hintLadder: Use the midpoint of A's emission and reception readings.
An ahead clock must have its offset subtracted from later readings.
Compute both transit durations before dividing distance by time.
